Norfolk State head coach Michael Vick is reversing course following his comments after his team’s 29-28 defeat to Norfolk State University during the postgame press conference. Vick dismissed his role in the botched victory formation that led to a fumble recovery and North Carolina Central’s game-winning score. But in comments made during Monday’s MEAC coaches’ call, Vick offered some perspective on what happened and said he made a mistake by putting his headset down. “Just to put it to rest. We practiced for a minute last week. We was in second and four, with a minute 30 or whatever was on the clock. I put the headset down, which was my mistake first and foremost. The one thing I learned is to stay on the headset, stay communicating and not think that the game is over. I said victory.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) He then explained what his offensive coordinator was thinking, and he said the two weren’t on the same page. “What our offensive coordinator was thinking was that we get the first down, run another run play, get the first down and finish the game with the offense on the field. And I totally understood. I understand it now what his logic was. I was thinking we was just gonna go into victory. They had no timeouts. Run the clock down to about 18 seconds, punt it off, and then play. They would’ve had to go 80 yards in 18 seconds or something like that. But we wasn’t on the same page, and that’s my mistake. That’s not his mistake. That’s my mistake for not staying on the headset and communicating what needs to happen up until the very second.” Vick said the responsibility is his and described what he should have told the coordinator. “If I ask my players to play all the way to the very end, till the clock strike triple zero, then I gotta coach until the clock strike triple zero. So that’s on me, it’s not on him. As a coordinator, he’s gonna do what he think is best, and it wasn’t communicated the right way. What I should have said was, ‘Coach, victory. That’s on me as the head coach to know every situation and make sure that I keep my headset on to think through situations as I’ve always done with our coordinators. item.title: Raducanu to return at January's United Cup after injury lay-off
item.description: Emma Raducanu missed Wimbledon and the US Open through injury [Getty Images] Emma Raducanu will make her return to tennis in the United Cup team competition in Australia in the first week of 2027. Britain's 2021 US Open champion has not played since June because of a stress fracture of the shin. Raducanu was beaten by Croatia’s Donna Vekic in her first grass-court final at Queen's Club on 14 June, but had to pull out of Wimbledon on the eve of her opening match just 14 days later. The 23-year-old contemplated playing a couple of events in Asia this autumn but, by delaying her return until January, she will be able to use a special ranking of 38 to enter tournaments. A special ranking is available to players who have been out with injury for at least six months. In Raducanu's case, it reflects her position in the world rankings after Wimbledon, as she received some prize money despite not playing a match there. The current British number five will be able to use a special ranking to enter eight events next year, including two Grand Slams and five WTA 1000 tournaments. Her actual ranking of 107 would likely be too low to make the main draw of January's Australian Open and most other WTA Tour events. But with a special ranking, Raducanu will not only be assured of playing in Melbourne but also at the WTA 1000 events in Doha, Dubai, Indian Wells and Miami which follow in February and March. The entry deadline for the United Cup passed on Monday, shortly after Raducanu had her application for a special ranking approved. A ranking of 38 will make her the British number one for the purposes of this event, giving her the chance to play alongside Arthur Fery in a competition featuring 18 national teams. Francesca Jones, Jan Choinski and doubles players Neal Skupski and Olivia Nicholls complete the British team for the tournament, which takes place from 1-10 January. Britain will play Australia and France in their group matches in Sydney, and Raducanu can expect to be face current top-40 players Talia Gibson and Diane Parry. 'I don't fear for my safety from online abuse - because we're so used to it' Raducanu made a gradual return to training in early September - and four months is a long time to train without any competitive action. She may also not play any exhibitions between now and the end of the year but a spell of warm weather training is anticipated, with the Middle East a popular destination for players in the run-up to the Australian Open. Recent practice sessions in London with head coach Andrew Richardson and LTA national coach Alex Ward have been increasing in intensity, according to observers. But by the time Raducanu returns, she will have been on the sidelines for over six months. item.title: GB and Wales' Griffiths banned after drug test
item.description: Josh Griffiths was the first British runner to cross the line at the 2017 London Marathon. [Getty Images] A Great Britain and Wales marathon runner, who shocked the elite to win a place at the World Championships, was banned after returning a positive drugs test. Josh Griffiths, 33, was given a three-month ban by the World Athletics' Athletics Integrity Unit (AIU) after Benzoylecgonine – which is found in the body when it processes cocaine - appeared in his system following May's Belfast City Marathon. Griffiths, who represented Great Britain at the 2017 and 2022 Worlds and ran for Wales at the 2018 Commonwealth Games, denied ever taking cocaine or any other social drug. He could not prove how cocaine entered his system, but in their ruling the AIU accepted that any ingestion was both out of competition and "unrelated to sport" as they imposed the ban. Griffiths' ban ran for three months from the hearing date of 19 June, 2026. In addition his race results from the day of the Belfast Marathon - 3 May - until the end of the ban were expunged. Following the findings, Griffiths accepted the anti-doping rule violation and the sanction. The Carmarthenshire athlete rose to prominence when he finished as the fastest Briton as a club runner in the 2017 London Marathon, earning him a place in the GB squad for that year's World Championships. He went on to record an eighth-place finish in London in 2021, having turned professional after the 2017 success. The AIU said in its their report that Griffiths remarked it was "absolutely impossible" when he was told of the initial adverse finding in his sample and that "there must have been a mistake". Benzoylecgonine, which is found in the body when it processes cocaine, appeared in both samples of urine provided following the Belfast marathon. Griffiths provided details of his activities and whereabouts leading up to the 3 May race, as well as his stay at the official race hotel, stressing he did not attend any social events, consume any alcohol and that contact had been mainly with other athletes and race staff. At a later hearing, he reiterated that he had never knowingly ingested cocaine and was not aware of anyone close to him using the drug in the lead-up to the Belfast race. Griffiths submitted scientific data to support his claim that any ingestion was out of competition, something the AIU went on to agree with.

item.title: What's the cost of slow play? LPGA stiffens fines, penalties for 2027 season
item.description: For all the penalty strokes that have been dished out over the past two seasons, the LPGA has gotten – slower. “The data told us we were heading in the wrong direction,” wrote LPGA player president Vicki Goetz-Ackerman in a memo send to players and caddies on Tuesday. While the median round times of threesomes was flat between 2025 and 2026 across nine different tournaments, twosomes were seven minutes slower this season (from 3:55 to 4:02). The total number of holes timed (over the course of 15 events) increased by 12 percent. And number of penalty strokes dished out also increased from seven to nine. Even those in contention were not spared . This fall, the Pace of Play committee met to discuss what could be done. When the more aggressive 2027 Pace of Play Policy was unveiled on Tuesday night at an LPGA player meeting, many in the room clapped. “I'm a big fan,” said speedy world No. 1 Nelly Korda, adding, “no one wants to be out here for five-plus hours. No player wants to. Nobody wants to watch it. I think we're just moving in the right direction.” That direction includes a bigger hit to the wallet. In 2026, players who were 1-5 seconds over time allotment received a $5,000 fine on the third occurrence. Now, there are no warnings. It’s a fine on the first offense. (First occurrence, $2,000; second occurrence, $4,000; third occurrence, $8,000). This season, those who were 6-15 seconds over, received a 1-stroke penalty. Now, it’s the penalty stroke, plus a fine. Those who are 16+ seconds over in 2027 will receive a 2-stroke penalty and a fine. Where the fines really increased, however, is in the repeat offender category. In 2026, those who were timed between 40-49 holes received a $5,000 fine, and it escalated from there. In 2027, players who have been timed an aggregate of 35 holes over the course of a season will receive a $35,000 fine, and it goes up from there (36-40 +$1,000 per hole; 41-45, +$2,000 per hole, etc.). In addition, the tour has shaved 10 seconds off the excessive shot time limit, going from 70 seconds to 60 seconds. Players who are currently serving on the POP committee include Allisen Corpuz, Lindy Duncan, Sofia Garcia, Jennifer Kupcho and Riley Smyth. “I think it’s great,” said veteran player Alison Lee. “I think it will make the LPGA a lot of money, and I think with how this is structured, it will actually force slow players to be more mindful about how much time they’re taking.” While the pace was quicker in 2025 when the initial changes were put into effect , the fact that things either flatlined or got worse, means the subject will be talked about more going forward. Pace of play has long been an issue on the LPGA, but it reached a pinnacle in 2024 at The Annika, when they missed the TV window by nearly an hour on Saturday. For two rounds, play spilled over into the next day without an interruption in play. The tour cut the field for the Annika from 120 to 108 in 2025. item.title: India pacer Arshdeep Singh, Samreen Kaur get engaged in New Zealand; pics go viral
item.description: Indian fast bowler Arshdeep Singh got engaged to actor-model Samreen Kaur in New Zealand on Wednesday, sharing pictures of his proposal on social media. The announcement came just hours after his high-profile move from Punjab Kings to Mumbai Indians ahead of the IPL 2027 season was confirmed. Samreen shared pictures of Arshdeep proposing to her, along with a heartfelt message celebrating their relationship. "And of all the things life could have given us, I'm the happiest it gave us each other. To a lifetime together. 11.11.2026 (Hi Fiance)," she wrote on Instagram. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Samreen (@samreenkaur__) The couple are currently in New Zealand, where Arshdeep is part of India's ODI squad. Their engagement comes nearly four months after the cricketer made their relationship public by sharing pictures with Samreen on July 26, captioning them "My Person". Who is Samreen Kaur? Samreen is an actor, model and social media personality from Jammu and Kashmir. She was a finalist in Femina Miss India 2018 and has appeared in projects such as the film '83, the ZEE5 series Nail Polish and Punjabi film Sardaar Ji 2. She has also featured in music videos with singers including Guru Randhawa, Badshah and Jubin Nautiyal. Arshdeep had earlier spoken about their relationship after dedicating his unique wicket celebration during the first ODI against New Zealand to Samreen. "That's for my girlfriend. We do these dance steps when we're out walking or something like that. Whenever the mood is a little low, we cheer each other up with that celebration," he said after taking four wickets. A big day in Arshdeep's career The engagement also coincided with a major IPL development, as Arshdeep was traded from Punjab Kings to Mumbai Indians in exchange for Hardik Pandya ahead of IPL 2027. Arshdeep will join Mumbai at his existing fee of Rs 18 crore. The 27-year-old had represented Punjab since his IPL debut in 2019, finishing his stint as the franchise's leading wicket-taker with 111 wickets in 96 matches.

item.title: Oregon star edge rusher Teitum Tuioti out for the season
item.description: EUGENE — One of Oregon football’s most important defensive players is done for the season. Ducks senior defensive end Teitum Tuioti suffered a season-ending knee injury in Oregon’s 41-28 win over Ohio State , Dan Lanning announced on Monday. “Teitum has been unbelievable for us this year, and every year he’s been here,” Lanning said. “Just watching him grow as a player and person has been a lot of fun for us. But unfortunately Teitum’s done for the year, he had a knee injury, he’ll end up having surgery.” Tuioti was among the Ducks’ leaders in tackles with 44, and ranked second on the team in sacks with 5.5 on the season. The former Sheldon High School star sits at No. 8 all-time for Oregon with 22.5 sacks across his four seasons, providing steady leadership on a talented and experienced defensive front. In the win over the Buckeyes, he also showed off his arm: Tuioti completed a pass to fellow defensive end Matayo Uiagalelei on a memorable fake punt which shifted momentum in the game. “I hate it for him, because (the injury) was a routine, weird play that it happened on,” Lanning said. “He left it on the line there on the field, and I don’t know if he’ll get another chance to play as an Oregon football player, but whoever gets to have that guy on their team in the future is gonna be really, really lucky.” Should Tuioti forgo his fifth year of eligibility and enter the NFL Draft, he is a projected second- or third-round pick according to some mock drafts. item.title: Who will call plays for Oregon after Mehringer's firing?
item.description: EUGENE — After firing first-year offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer seven games into the 2026 season, Dan Lanning shared Oregon ’s plans for filling his role moving forward at his weekly press conference Monday night. Offensive assistant Jay Johnson will lead offensive playcalling for the Ducks going forward, Lanning said. “He has a lot of experience as a play-caller, was with me in Georgia when we were part of the national championship team,” Lanning said. “Went on to have a lot of success in Colorado and Michigan State. He’s gonna lead the efforts there with the offensive staff, but it’ll still be a collaborative effort, with a lot of the work that we do. “He’s also coming in with a different perspective, a different view, not being with us the last few years, where he can provide a couple things that might be different than what we’ve done.” Mehringer, previously the tight ends coach for the Ducks, is the first assistant coach Lanning has fired in his tenure at Oregon, which began in 2022. The Ducks’ offensive decision-making was at the center of intense criticism over the past three weeks, during which Oregon averaged just 14 points per game and lost twice to UCLA and Illinois. Lanning spoke to the human element of letting Mehringer go. “They see the football coach, right? That’s also an unbelievable dad. A great husband,” Lanning said. “The guy’s been part of our staff for the last five years, that’s done some really good things here, and I think all of us feel like we shoulder some of the blame. item.title: Lanning: Stewart incident 'didn't match our standard'
item.description: EUGENE — After Oregon wide receiver Evan Stewart was booked in Springfield Municipal Jail early Sunday morning on DUII charges, Ducks coach Dan Lanning addressed the situation at his weekly press conference Monday. “There was an incident this weekend that didn’t match our standard here in our program,” Lanning said. “There will be an appropriate action taken. Still gathering some details with what that situation looks like. But that would be handled internally. I’m not gonna respond to any other questions about that. We’re gonna handle that with our guys. “There’s an expectation of what you have to... how you have to act, and how you need to perform in our program. Kind of overshadows the success that we had on Saturday, which is disappointing, but that will be handled by us internally. I’m not going to speak on it publicly.” When Lanning was asked a follow-up question about a rumored speeding incident involving other Oregon football players, for which there haven’t been any confirmed arrests, he said, “I was talking about the same thing when I first addressed it.” This is also the second instance of an Oregon football team member facing DUII charges in the past year. In April, running backs coach Ra’Shaad Samples allegedly backed his Ford F-150 into a parked car outside a bar in Eugene. His next court date is Oct. 27. An arraignment for Stewart in his DUII case hasn’t been set, as official charges haven’t been filed to Springfield Municipal Court as of Monday evening, according to court records. Stewart leads the Ducks this season with 27 catches for 352 yards and four touchdowns. He missed Saturday’s win over Nebraska due to an undisclosed injury. item.title: Host shocked by sports radio caller from hospital delivery room
item.description: Credit: Bill Streicher-USA TODAY Sports, USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Over the years, we have seen dedicated sports radio callers that went above and beyond the call of duty. Sports radio callers are a different breed of humanity. We’ve seen calls from both sides of the law whether it’s cops giving traffic stops or prisoners . There are epic personalities like Miss Lisa from Arkansas and longtime regulars that become beloved fixtures like the legendary Chris in Syracuse and Phyllis from Mulga . But Tuesday night’s clash between the Philadelphia 76ers and Boston Celtics, featuring the first meeting with Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown on opposite sides of the floor, featured a call that is a first-ballot Hall of Famer. Corey in Germantown called into 94WIP from the hospital delivery room with his newborn baby audibly crying in the background. I still can’t believe this happened. For those who missed it, the full Corey in Germantown phone call into my show on @SportsRadioWIP last night: https://t.co/Qgpz4TwNYQ — Buzz (@BuzzWIP) November 11, 2026 “I’m at the hospital with me and my wife, having our baby, having our daughter,” Corey started. Host Daniel “Buzz” Wilson was stunned, asking if that was Corey’s newborn crying in the background. He then said that his daughter was born at 9:10 p.m. ET during the Sixers-Celtics game and the WIP show. But the doctors and nurses can handle the newborn. Corey had to talk about the game. “I want to talk to you about Paul George. I don’t like Paul George. I like and I hate Pritchard, he’s annoying. I hate him. I wish we had more players like that,” Corey said. Corey then admitted he was back and forth with locking in on the game and the birth of his daughter. In fairness, his wife was the one doing all the work, but it would be great to also hear from his wife regarding her thoughts about how much he was paying attention to the game and how much he was supporting her through the miracle of childbirth. Wilson summed up the surreal nature of the call after it ended. “That baby that you heard in the background there did not exist when the game started tonight. When my show started tonight, that baby did not exist. And even though the baby was born around halftime, he just called in with Paul George takes from tonight’s game,” Wilson said. Congratulations to the presumably still happy couple on the birth of their newborn child. And we look forward to her following in her father’s footsteps and calling in to WIP when she’s able to utter her first words to talk about how Nick Sirianni needs to go. item.title: Top-ranked Bethlehem boys' soccer has state championship in its sights
item.description: Bethlehem senior Orson Wagg gets a head on the ball during the Section 2, Class AA finals against Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake on Saturday, Oct. 31, 2026, at LaSalle Institute in Troy, NY. (Jim Franco/Times Union) (Jim Franco/Times Union) DELMAR - Despite an undefeated regular season, getting through the final stages of the Section 2 Class AA playoffs was a bit of a slog for the Bethlehem boys' soccer team. In the semifinals, the Eagles were held to a scoreless draw after 110 minutes against a Niskayuna team they'd beaten by nine goals a month earlier, but advanced on penalty kicks . The championship game was settled in regulation, a 1-0 win over Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake , but beating the Spartans was no easy task either. But when Bethlehem got out of Section 2 this past weekend for a NYSPHSAA regional final against Section 3's Watertown, everything seemed to click back into place in a 2-0 win over a previously undefeated team that entered the game ranked first in the state. "We played the way we wanted to, and we played up to our standard," said senior Ayaz Sajid , who scored both goals in the win that clinched the Eagles' berth in the state semifinals , where they'll face Section 5's Churchville-Chili on Saturday at 10:45 a.m. at Middletown High School. Bethlehem (16-0-3 overall) coach Brian Spina believes that getting to face a less familiar opponent allowed the Eagles to play their game with more freedom and comfort. "I think it's easier to play teams you haven't played before, in some respects -- or teams from out of the area -- because they don't really know your guys as much," Spina said. "Our guys, growing up playing club around this area, they've played against all these teams from our section a lot. I think our guys being able to go out of section, we were able to find some moments that they weren't able to find in the past few games." For the most part this season, the Eagles have been head-and-shoulders above their competition . Nine of their 16 wins this season have come by at least three goals, and the Bethlehem defense has surrendered just eight goals all season, with 14 shutouts. Bethlehem's win over Watertown also handed the No. 1 state ranking in Class AA to the Eagles, but that's an afterthought for a team set on leaving Middletown this weekend having proved on the pitch that they're the state's No. 1 team. Many of Bethlehem's players were part of the Eagles squad that reached the state final four in 2024, only to be bounced 2-0 by Clarence in the semifinals despite largely controlling the run of play. "We had a really good game (against Clarence)," Spina said. "To be honest, it was just a matter of not finishing our chances. … We just couldn't finish. item.title: How Jon Rahm's remarkable renaissance has set up Race to Dubai finale for the ages
item.description: Luke Donald may have had a little smile to himself when he examined the top of the leaderboard at last week’s Abu Dhabi Championship . The penultimate event of the DP World Tour season saw Jon Rahm come in from the cold to win his first event on the tour (excluding majors) in four years, fellow former LIV Golf exile Tyrrell Hatton finish second and Rory McIlroy come home third. Three of European Ryder Cup captain Donald’s most important players dominating one of their home tour’s biggest events – with the promise of more battles to come over the next 10 months before the 2027 showdown with the US at Adare Manor – bodes awfully well. It’s an exciting time for the DP World Tour, with the demise of LIV Golf meaning that many of the sport’s big names, from both Europe and overseas, who would otherwise be playing elsewhere next year will be plying their trade on the circuit formerly known as the European Tour. A rejuvenated Jon Rahm won in Abu Dhabi last week (AP) Leaderboards as star-studded as the Abu Dhabi Championship will become more commonplace, attracting more eyeballs to the tour and giving homegrown players a much more regular taste of elite competition. In that vein, this week’s $10m DP World Tour Championship at the Earth Course in Dubai could be the most exciting finale to the Race to Dubai – the tour’s season-long order of merit – for many years. McIlroy vs Rahm vs Eugenio Chacarra vs Patrick Reed vs Aaron Rai vs Ryan Fox . It has the perfect blend of global superstars who are in good form (Rahm and McIlroy), two more recent major winners (Rai and Fox), a pantomime villain (Reed) and an up-and-coming European talent who has had a superb season and is now trying to hold off the big horses charging from behind (Chacarra). And if you have a soft spot for true outsiders, you’ll be pleased to know that even Casey Jarvis, Jayden Schaper and Daniel Hillier still have a mathematical chance of taking the crown should they win the tournament and other results fall in their favour – making it a nine-way battle. Seven-time Race to Dubai winner (including each of the last four) McIlroy must be the favourite, with only he and the much more unproven Chacarra being in the enviable position of knowing that winning the DP World Tour Championship guarantees victory in the order of merit regardless of everyone else’s results. The Northern Irishman will also match Colin Montgomerie for the all-time record of eight if he gets over the line this weekend. item.title: Have the Saints finally cleaned up their discipline issues?
item.description: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - NOVEMBER 08: Chris Olave #12 of the New Orleans Saints reacts during the fourth quarter of a game against the Cleveland Browns at Caesars Superdome on November 08, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Morgan Simmons/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New Orleans Saints have spent much of the season making life harder on themselves with costly penalties. Whether it’s been extending opposing drives, putting the offense behind the chains or simply failing to execute when it matters most, discipline has been a consistent concern. However, Sunday’s win over the Cleveland Browns gave fans a reason to believe things might finally be moving in the right direction. The Saints finished the day with just four penalties for 25 yards, a big improvement from what we’ve seen throughout the first half of the season. The Saints have struggled to avoid those self-inflicted setbacks, making Sunday’s performance a refreshing change. Coming out of the bye week, there was an opportunity for Kellen Moore, his coaching staff and the players to address some of the issues that have held them back. Still, it would be an overreaction to say the Saints have officially solved their problems. One game, regardless of how encouraging it was, doesn’t take back the mistakes that have continued to show up throughout the first half of the season. Consistency is key in the NFL, and it’s beyond time for Kellen Moore and New Orleans to prove they can maintain this level of discipline moving forward. The encouraging part is that the Saints showed they are capable of playing a much cleaner game. It’s too early to say the issue fixed, but it is certainly fair to believe the bye week helped to some degree. Now the challenge is making Sunday’s discipline the expectation rather than the exception.

At the time, Reed was the first LIV star since Brooks Koepka to ditch the upstart league for a return to pro golf’s conventional career track. It turned out to be a wise move. Reed did not receive a special exemption to return to the PGA Tour in 2026, as Koepka did, so he took the matter into his own hands. Within a few weeks of his LIV exit, Reed won two DP World Tour events to rocket into first place in the Race to Dubai rankings . The top 10 players in the Race to Dubai at season’s end earn their PGA Tour cards. With one tournament to go, Reed sits in third. He has a great chance to win the title, but either way, he’s already secured his 2027 PGA Tour return. News 'It would mean a lot': Patrick Reed aims to spoil Rory McIlroy's shot at history By: Kevin Cunningham That’s an enviable position in which to be, especially compared to Reed’s former LIV compatriots who decided to stick with the upstart league in 2026. Now LIV Golf is no more , and, unlike Reed, those players are scrambling to find playing opportunities for next year while serving lengthy PGA Tour bans. But in his pre-tournament press conference at this week’s DP World Tour Championship, Reed explained that he gets no “satisfaction” out of the fact that so many LIV players are stuck in difficult situations following the league’s demise, while he is making PGA Tour plans for 2027. The 2018 Masters champion also revealed serious ambitions for both his PGA Tour and, potentially, Ryder Cup returns next year. Patrick Reed on beating other LIV pros back to PGA Tour: ‘I don’t really get any satisfaction’ Make no mistake about it, Reed is pleased with his decision to leave LIV earlier this year before the league went under. He’s also proud of himself for putting the work in and earning his way back to the PGA Tour the hard way. “The year has been very satisfying, and really, I’ve kind of reflected a little bit on it the past couple weeks, on kind of going out there,” Reed said. “And rankings don’t really mean anything at the beginning of the year, throughout the year and everything like that. It’s about going out there and getting the job done.” With wins at the Hero Dubai Desert Classic in late January and the Qatar Masters in early February , Reed did just that, virtually earning his 2027 PGA Tour card before winter had ended. News 'No lawsuits anymore': Patrick Reed has earned Rory McIlroy's 'respect' post-LIV exit By: Josh Schrock “To kind of make that step and make the opportunity, to have to finish in the top 10 to earn my spot on the PGA Tour, and basically come out and believe in myself and put all my eggs in one basket and go get the job done means a lot,” Reed said.
